name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the newest *open* PR first. It’s the fastest way to catch issues before they compound, and open PRs are where fresh mistakes live. The trade-off is ignoring older merged PRs, but speed beats completeness here—we can circle back later if needed. This keeps the improvement loop tight and avoids wasting time on stale reviews.

name: Gauge
text: Shadow mode on the newest *open* PR risks missing systemic issues buried in older merged PRs—those are where patterns compound. A better alternative: run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the oldest merged PR first, then expand to newer ones; this surfaces legacy edge cases before they infect fresh work. Settle it by measuring the rate of new vs. legacy issues caught in a 2-week trial.
